sources.title: 2025 Birth Statistics
sources.publisher: Republic of Korea Ministry of Data and Statistics / National Data Office (Aug. 26, 2026)
supports: second consecutive annual fertility increase after 0.72 in 2023 and 0.75 in 2024
sources.limits: Use the agency release for the annual total; avoid treating two years of rebound as proof of a durable reversal.

sources.title: Population Trends Survey: Marriage statistics
sources.publisher: Statistics Korea / Ministry of Data and Statistics
sources.limits: Marriage is a leading correlate of births in Korea, not a sufficient causal explanation for fertility change.

sources.title: East Asia's Coming Population Collapse
sources.limits: Single demographer's analysis/opinion, not an official statistical release; present as a projection and balance against contrary views.

sources.title: Preliminary Counts of the 2025 Population Census of Japan
sources.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (released May 29, 2026; bulletin June 25, 2026)
supports: 123.05 million total population as of Oct. 1, 2025
Tokyo metropolitan area 36.986 million / 30.1% of Japan
sources.limits: The agency explicitly labels these preliminary counts; manuscript should not call them final census totals.

sources.title: Nagoro, Japan's scarecrow village
sources.limits: Human-interest travel journalism; population figures vary slightly by outlet and should not carry broader demographic claims.

sources.title: Statistical Communiqué of the People's Republic of China on the 2025 National Economic and Social Development
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China (Feb. 28, 2026)
sources.limits: NBS does not report the chapter's approximately 0.93 total-fertility-rate estimate in this release; attribute that estimate externally or omit it.

sources.title: China's fertility rate has fallen to one, continuing a long decline that began before and continued after the one-child policy
supports: fertility decline predates the 1980 one-child policy
decline continued after the 2015/2016 and 2021 policy reversals
sources.limits: Useful counterevidence against monocausal one-child-policy explanations; not a primary Chinese statistical release.

sources.title: World Population Prospects 2024: Summary of Results
supports: peak around 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s
80% estimated probability of an in-century peak
sources.limits: Projection, not observation; uncertainty ranges matter and later revisions may move in either direction.

sources.title: Peak global population and other key findings from the 2024 UN World Population Prospects
supports: comparison of recent UN projection rounds
2024 revision moved the expected peak lower and earlier relative to earlier projections
sources.limits: Use revision history as evidence that forecasts change, not as evidence that future revisions must continue in the same direction.

sources.title: Fertility, mortality, migration, and population scenarios for 195 countries and territories from 2017 to 2100
sources.limits: Scenario-based projection with assumptions that differ materially from UN DESA; the disagreement is evidence of model uncertainty.
